参考范文

Dear Club Members,

I am writing to recommend a book for our next reading session: The Old Man and the Sea by Ernest Hemingway.

I recommend it for three reasons. First, it is a concise yet profound novella that can be finished within a few hours. Second, Hemingway's distinctive "iceberg" style leaves much to discuss in terms of language and symbolism. Finally, the story of the old fisherman's struggle against a giant marlin conveys a timeless spirit of perseverance that inspires every reader. I hope you will enjoy reading it.

Yours sincerely, Li Ming

【译文】

各位书友：

我写信是想为咱们下期的读书会推荐一本书：欧内斯特·海明威的《老人与海》。

推荐它有三点理由。首先，这是一部凝练而深刻的中篇，几小时便可读完。其次，海明威独特的"冰山"风格在语言与象征上极富讨论空间。最后，老渔夫与巨鱼搏斗的故事传递出永恒的不屈精神，激励着每一位读者。希望你们读得开心。

谨上，李明

参考范文

The cartoon depicts four people seated around a dinner table laden with food, yet each is bowing their head over a smartphone, exchanging no words with one another. The caption reads: a party in the age of mobile phones.

The drawing reveals a common malady of modern life: while mobile phones bring us unprecedented convenience, they are quietly alienating us from those around us. Many young people stare at screens even during family dinners or gatherings with friends, treating physical companionship as mere background noise. Left unchecked, this habit will erode genuine human bonds and leave our relationships hollow.

From my perspective, phones are tools, not masters. We should learn to put them aside when we are with family and friends. Only by treasuring face-to-face communication can we maintain authentic emotional ties and build a warmer society.

Just how much does the Constitution protect your digital data? The Supreme Court will now consider whether police can search the contents of a mobile phone without a warrant if the phone is on or around a person during an arrest.

宪法究竟在多大程度上保护你的数字数据？最高法院将审议：警察在逮捕时，若手机在嫌疑人身上或附近，能否在没有搜查令的情况下查看手机内容。

California has asked the justices to refrain from a sweeping ruling, particularly one that upsets the old assumption that authorities may search through the possessions of suspects at the time of their arrest. It is hard, the state argues, for judges to assess the implications of new and rapidly changing technologies.

加州已请求大法官们避免做出一刀切的裁决，尤其是那种打破"当局可在逮捕时搜查嫌疑人财物"这一旧假设的裁决。该州认为，法官很难评估快速变化的新技术所带来的影响。

The court would be recklessly modest if it followed California's advice. Enough of the implications are discernable, even obvious, so that the justices can and should provide updated guidelines to police, lawyers and defendants.

如果最高法院听从加州的建议，那将是不负责任的保守。其影响已经足够清晰，甚至显而易见，大法官们能够也应该向警察、律师和被告提供更新后的指导方针。

They should start by discarding California's lame argument that exploring the contents of a smartphone—a vast storehouse of digital information—is similar to, say, going through a suspect's purse. The court has ruled that police don't violate the Fourth Amendment when they go through the wallet or pocketbook of an arrestee without a warrant. But exploring one's smartphone is more like entering his or her home. A smartphone may contain an arrestee's reading history, financial history, medical history and comprehensive records of recent correspondence. The development of "cloud computing," meanwhile, has made that exploration so much the easier.

他们首先应该摒弃加州那个站不住脚的论点——即查看智能手机（一个庞大的数字信息库）内容类似于翻查嫌疑人的钱包。最高法院曾裁定，警察在没有搜查令的情况下翻看被捕者的钱包不算违反第四修正案。但查看智能手机更像是进入一个人的家。一部智能手机可能包含被捕者的阅读史、财务史、医疗史以及近期通信的完整记录。与此同时，"云计算"的发展使这种查看变得更加容易。

Americans should take steps to protect their digital privacy. But keeping sensitive information on these devices is increasingly a requirement of normal life. Citizens still have a right to expect private documents to remain private and protected by the Constitution's prohibition on unreasonable searches.

美国人应该采取措施保护他们的数字隐私。但在这些设备上保存敏感信息日益成为正常生活的需要。公民仍然有权期待私人文件保持私密，并受宪法禁止无理搜查条款的保护。

As so often is the case, stating that principle doesn't ease the challenge of line-drawing. In many cases, it would not be overly burdensome for authorities to obtain a warrant to search through phone contents. They could still invalidate Fourth Amendment protections when facing severe, urgent circumstances, and they could take reasonable measures to ensure that phone data are not erased or altered while waiting for a warrant. The court, though, may want to allow room for police to cite situations where they are entitled to more freedom.

Integrity had collapsed, she argued, because of a collective acceptance that the only "sorting mechanism" in society should be profit and the market. But "it's us, human beings, we the people who create the society we want, not profit." 两年前，鲁伯特·默多克的女儿伊丽莎白谈到"我们众多机构中诚信令人不安地缺失"。她认为，诚信已经崩塌，因为人们普遍接受社会唯一的"分选机制"应该是利润和市场。但"创造我们想要的社会的，是我们人类自己，而不是利润。" Driving her point home, she continued: "It's increasingly apparent that the absence of purpose, of a moral language within government, media or business could become one of the most dangerous goals for capitalism and freedom." This same absence of moral purpose was wounding companies such as News International, she thought, making it more likely that it would lose its way as it had with widespread illegal telephone hacking. 为进一步阐明观点，她继续说道："政府、媒体或商界内部缺乏道德目标和道德语言，这一点日益明显，可能成为资本主义和自由最危险的目标之一。"她认为，同样的道德目标缺失正在损害新闻国际等公司，使其更可能像在大规模非法电话窃听事件中那样迷失方向。 As the hacking trial concludes—finding guilty one ex-editor of the News of the World, Andy Coulson, for conspiring to hack phones, and finding his predecessor, Rebekah Brooks, innocent of the same charge—the wider issue of dearth of integrity still stands. Journalists are known to have hacked the phones of up to 5,500 people. This is hacking on an industrial scale, as was acknowledged by Glenn Mulcaire, the man hired by the News of the World in 2001 to be the point person for phone hacking. Others await trial. This long story still unfolds. 随着窃听审判的结束——《世界新闻报》前编辑安迪·库尔森因合谋窃听电话被判有罪，而其前任丽贝卡·布鲁克斯在同一指控中被判无罪——更广泛的诚信缺失问题依然存在。已知记者窃听了多达5500人的电话。这是工业规模的窃听，正如格伦·穆尔凯尔所承认的那样，他是《世界新闻报》2001年聘用的电话窃听负责人。其他人还在等待审判。这一漫长的故事仍在展开。 In many respects, the dearth of moral purpose frames not only the fact of such widespread phone hacking but the terms on which the trial took place. One of the astonishing revelations was how little Rebekah Brooks knew of what went on in her newsroom, how little she thought to ask and the fact that she never inquired how the stories arrived. The core of her successful defence was that she knew nothing. 在许多方面，道德目标的缺失不仅构成了这种大规模电话窃听的事实，也构成了审判进行的条件。令人震惊的揭露之一是，丽贝卡·布鲁克斯对其编辑部发生的事情知之甚少，她几乎没想过问，也从未询问新闻是如何得来的。她成功辩护的核心就是她一无所知。 In today's world, it has become normal that well-paid executives should not be accountable for what happens in the organisations that they run. Perhaps we should not be so surprised. For a generation, the collective doctrine has been that the sorting mechanism of society should be profit. The words that have mattered are efficiency, flexibility, shareholder value, business-friendly, wealth generation, sales, impact and, in newspapers, circulation. Words degraded to the margin have been justice, fairness, tolerance, proportionality and accountability. 在当今世界，高薪高管不对自己所运营组织中发生的事情负责，这已成为常态。也许我们不该如此惊讶。对于一代人来说，集体信条一直是社会的分选机制应该是利润。重要的词汇是效率、灵活性、股东价值、有利商业、财富创造、销售额、影响力，以及在报业中的发行量。被边缘化的词汇则是正义、公平、宽容、相称和问责。 The purpose of editing the News of the World was not to promote reader understanding, to be fair in what was written or to betray any common humanity. It was to ruin lives in the quest for circulation and impact. Ms Brooks may or may not have had suspicions about how her journalists got their stories, but she asked no questions, gave no instructions—nor received traceable, recorded answers. 《世界新闻报》的编辑目的不是增进读者理解、公正报道或流露任何共同人性。它的目的是在追求发行量和影响力的过程中毁掉人们的生活。布鲁克斯女士可能怀疑、也可能不怀疑她的记者是如何得到新闻的，但她没有问任何问题，没有给出任何指示——也没有收到可追溯、有记录的回答。

partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G

options.label: A
options.en: Are we studying that text and trying to respond in a way that fulfils the requirement of a given course? Reading it simply for pleasure? Skimming it for information? Ways of reading on a train or in bed are likely to differ considerably from reading in a seminar room.
options.zh: 我们是在研读那篇文本、并试图以某种满足某门课程要求的方式作出回应吗？还是仅仅为了愉悦而读？或是略读以获取信息？在火车上或床上阅读的方式，很可能与在研讨室里阅读大不相同。

options.label: B
options.en: Factors such as the place and period in which we are reading, our gender, ethnicity, age and social class will encourage us towards certain interpretation but at the same time obscure or even close off others.
options.zh: 我们阅读的场所与时期、我们的性别、族裔、年龄和社会阶层等因素，会引导我们趋向某些解读，但同时也会遮蔽甚至封闭另一些解读。

options.label: C
options.en: If you are unfamiliar with words or idioms, you guess at their meaning, using clues presented in the context. On the assumption that they will become relevant later, you make a mental note of discourse entities as well as possible links between them.
options.zh: 如果你不熟悉某些词语或习语，你会借助语境提供的线索去猜测其义。基于它们日后会变得相关的假设，你会在脑中记下话语实体以及它们之间可能的联系。

options.label: D
options.en: In effect, you try to reconstruct the likely meanings or effects that any given sentence, image or reference might have had: These might be the ones the author intended.
options.zh: 实际上，你试图重构任何一个特定句子、意象或指涉可能具有的含义或效果：这些可能正是作者所意图的。

options.label: E
options.en: You make further inferences, for instance, about how the text may be significant to you, or about its validity—inferences that form the basis of a personal response for which the author will inevitably be far less responsible.
options.zh: 你会作出进一步的推断，例如关于该文本可能对你有何意义，或关于其有效性——这些推断构成了个人回应的基础，而作者对其所负的责任必然小得多。

options.label: F
options.en: In plays, novels and narrative poems, characters speak as constructs created by the author, not necessarily as mouthpieces for the author's own thoughts.
options.zh: 在戏剧、小说和叙事诗中，人物是作为作者所创造的建构在说话，而不一定是作者自身思想的传声筒。

options.label: G
options.en: Rather, we ascribe meanings to text on the basis of interaction between what we might call textual and contextual material: between kinds of organization or patterning we perceive in a text's formal structures (so especially its language structures) and various kinds of background, social knowledge, belief and attitude that we bring to the text.
options.zh: 毋宁说，我们是在所谓文本材料与语境材料的互动基础上赋予文本以意义：即我们在文本形式结构（尤其是其语言结构）中感知到的某种组织方式或模式，与我们带入文本的各类背景、社会知识、信念和态度之间的互动。
